title: Phased sampling middleware for onboarding stable model profiles
creator: Ayesha Rao
description: Introduce a lightweight, deterministic sampling middleware in the benchmark harness to produce phased performance profiles during model onboarding. Middleware will coordinate dataset slicing, prompt variant weighting, and runner affinity to generate stable, publishable profiles that respect version pinning and runtime SLO constraints.
background: Current profile generation has variability across runs due to non-deterministic sampling, uneven prompt variant coverage, and runner allocation noise. This causes flakey profile publications and noisy regressions during model onboarding. PMs and ML onboarding engineers need predictable profiles for version pinning and rollout decisions.
proposed_solution:
Build a middleware layer that plugs into the harness runner stack. Features:
- Deterministic seed bank and per-profile seed manifest
- Phased sampling plan: warmup, representative, tail-heavy
- Weighting rules for prompt variants derived from production telemetry (token distributions, common completions)
- Runner affinity tags so certain probes exercise KV cache / batching hot paths
- Profile publisher hook that annotates output with model-version pins and sampling manifest
- Fallback behavior: if a runner type is unavailable, substitute with compatible runner and add variance metadata
The middleware will expose a sampling manifest JSON (for the profile publisher) and a stable run-id to allow reproducible replays.
tradeoffs: Pros: much more stable profiles, easier diffs for performance regressions, clearer version pin recommendations. Cons: initial engineering cost to collect telemetry-derived weights; risk of overfitting profiles to observed traffic if we overweight a few prompt types. Operationally, increased complexity in harness configuration and requirement to maintain seed bank integrity.
tasks: Design sampling manifest schema and seed bank format (contrib: Research/PM)
Extend runner adapter interface with affinity tags and compatibility checks
Implement middleware that materializes phased sampling (warmup/rep/ tail) and deterministic RNG
Integrate telemetry lookup to produce prompt-variant weights (configurable override)
Expose profile-publisher hook to attach sampling_manifest and pinned_model metadata
End-to-end integration test with harness CI and a small on-prem runner pool
Prepare migration guide and CLI flags for backwards compatibility
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed for deterministic seed bank format. Prototype uses 64-bit salted seed per run. Recorded in docs/confluence/sampling-seeds (link below).
2026-03-05: API sketch for runner affinity reviewed with infra eng. Decided on three affinity levels: cache-hot, cold-path, and GPU-shared. Carlos to file small adapter changes PR.

2026-03-08: PM requested a phased plan that includes a short warmup to populate KV caches before measuring steady-state. Adjusted phase durations to 5% warmup, 85% representative, 10% tail by default.

2026-03-11: Ran test harness against model v1.3.2 and observed 18% reduction in profile variance for median latency across five runs. Captured artifacts and sent to perf-dashboard for deeper analysis.
review_comments: PM (Lina Cho): Ensure sampling weights remain editable by release engineers to avoid accidental coupling to production anomalies.
Design (Marco Ibarra): Add UX safe-guards in Console when pinning versions derived from a single phased profile (recommendation: require 3 independent publish runs or increase sample size).
Security (Priya Nair): Seed bank file contains no customer data; confirm audit logs for seed usage and publishing events.
Infra (Jamal Ortiz): Runner affinity must gracefully degrade when shared GPU pools are under high contention—prefer asynchronous substitution and variance tagging over blocking failures.
acceptance_criteria: Middleware emits sampling_manifest that includes seed, phase durations, prompt-variant weights, and runner affinity tags
Published profile artifacts include sampling_manifest and pinned_model metadata
End-to-end runs show <= 20% coefficient of variation for median latency across 5 consecutive publishes for representative workloads
Fallback substitution is exercised in CI matrix and results annotated with variance metadata
Migration flags allow existing harness users to opt-in without breaking current profiles
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic RNG, integration tests for phased sampling plan, e2e runs against a canary runner pool, and CI job that validates profile stabilization metrics. Add an automated replay job that can re-run a previously published manifest to validate reproducibility.
notes: Make sure sampling_manifest schema is forward-compatible. Consider adding a compact checksum for seed bank entries to detect accidental mutations. Coordinate with ML onboarding team for recommended default weights.
